articles.title: Whisky galore – and now plenty more besides: exploring the Scottish island of Islay
articles.summary: Distilleries are the backbone of Islay’s economy and tourist trade. Thanks to their success, other businesses – from breweries and farms to restaurants and chocolatiers – are now thriving and adding to the island’s appeal.
body: The Paps of Jura disappear into the mist as I pedal along the shores of Loch Indaal, and the rain cloud I’ve been racing finally catches up. I stash my hire bike at Port Charlotte youth hostel, quickly change and make it to Lochindaal Seafood Kitchen just before the downpour.

I’m soon warmed, by the welcome then by a bowl of creamy fish chowder. “We’ve plenty of fresh seafood just in,” is all the temptation I need to order the seafood plate. It’s a bowl for one, but a hungry one, and soon I’m picking and cracking my way through piles of fat langoustines and crab claws, with hot whisky-butter scallops and plenty of bread and butter.

The island of Islay, off the west coast of Scotland, is far better known for its drinks than its food. With 10, soon to be 11, working whisky distilleries, Islay is synonymous with rich, heavily peated single malts. But, over several days cycling around the island, I find that whisky does much more than fill warehouses and attract tourists. It is helping to support an island where agriculture, fishing and hospitality have long struggled to provide year-round employment.
points: Distilleries are the backbone of Islay’s economy and tourist trade.
Thanks to their success, other businesses – from breweries and farms to restaurants and chocolatiers – are now thriving and adding to the island’s appeal.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: I had a panic attack on public transport – and it led me to a horrifying secret
articles.summary: For a decade I lived with a fear so bad that I once tried to climb out of a tube carriage while it was in motion. Then a hypnotherapist told me to ask my parents one very important question. In 2000, I had been living in London for just over a decade and working at EMI Records for five years.
body: As things got progressively worse, I had a string of distressing panic attacks. Every time, it felt like the world around me was closing in. Then, in July 2003, during my daily commute between Brixton and the South Bank, I had a panic attack so intense I tried to climb out of the tube carriage doors. Thankfully, other passengers held me back until we arrived at the next platform – but I knew the problem was no longer something I could ignore.

The following year, my GP referred me to a hypnotherapist. During regression hypnotherapy sessions, I would sit on a chair, close my eyes and feel as if I was falling back through time to different points in my life. After three months of retracing old memories, my therapist asked me plainly if I had ever been in a train crash. “No, I think I’d know if I’d been in a train crash,” I said, slightly taken aback. Despite my insistence, she asked if I would double-check with my parents next time I saw them, in case I had been too young to remember.
points: For a decade I lived with a fear so bad that I once tried to climb out of a tube carriage while it was in motion.
Then a hypnotherapist told me to ask my parents one very important question.

articles.title: It’s not easy to show my scars. But I am proud to break the deadly silence around breast cancer in Nigeria | Gloria Chinyere Okwu
articles.summary: I was told to keep my diagnosis private but I am determined to show the reality of breast cancer and reject the stigma that prevents women seeking treatment. ‘Madam, this looks like breast cancer, and if it is, we will chop off your breast.” That was how the doctor welcomed me into the chaotic…
body: For a moment, I could no longer hear him. I thought of my three children, the university degree I had just bagged and the future I had envisaged. If I was going to die, what was the point of it all? I had invested everything I had to obtain that degree, subjecting my children to days of absence while I spent my nights in the university library.

The biopsy result was ready in seven days and the doctor was right: the next course of action was a mastectomy. Everyone had an opinion. My mother insisted a medicine man could heal me and begged me to cancel the scheduled surgery. My friends dragged me to churches because all I needed was prayers to be healed. As the surgery drew near, their voices grew louder. I was berated for lack of faith.

I had been told that the mastectomy was the solution and, after that, I could focus on my life again. That turned out not to be entirely true. A few days after my mastectomy, a group of doctors stood by my bedside and informed me that I would need further treatment, including chemotherapy.

articles.title: How Des Kohan Became LA’s Under-the-Radar Fashion Power Player
articles.summary: Desiree Kohan’s boutique takes an anti-trend approach to fashion at a time when algorithms determine what we wear more than ever. Designers and customers are embracing the model.
body: For the last 21 years in Los Angeles, Desiree Kohan’s boutique, Des Kohan, has been a destination for fashion discovery. And this September, she will do something she hasn’t felt compelled to do in years: go to New York Fashion Week.

Kohan has never made the seasonal circuit a priority, but a group of independent female designers she believes in — Ashlynn Park of Ashlyn, Maria McManus, and Alissa Zachary of High Sport — has become increasingly important to the mix at Des Kohan. Ashlyn and McManus will show in New York, while High Sport plans to present its collection digitally.

“I feel that they’re being authentic to who they are, and they’re all three unique,” Kohan says. Their approach reminds her of advice Dries Van Noten once offered on how to grow her store slowly with loyal partners. “That’s how these designers are.”
points: Desiree Kohan’s boutique takes an anti-trend approach to fashion at a time when algorithms determine what we wear more than ever.

articles.title: Poppy O’Toole’s midweek timesavers: spicy chicken and baked rice, and Thai-style lemongrass fishcakes – recipe
articles.summary: You’ll thank yourself for making these batch-cooking beauties to store in the freezer until the next busy worknight. I’ve called this spicy chicken and baked rice “midweek”, but you can enjoy this baby all week long.
body: Serving suggestions (optional) Sliced or pickled red onion Crumbled feta Flat-leaf parsley leaves In a bowl, combine the yoghurt, lemon zest and juice, harissa, garlic granules, dried oregano, ground turmeric, ras el hanout, coriander and cumin with a large pinch each of salt and pepper. Add the chicken thighs, give them a good mix to coat, then pop them in the fridge to marinate for at least an hour.

Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6. Meanwhile, put a glug of olive oil in an oven-safe saute pan on a high heat. Chuck in the onions and peppers, fry for two to three minutes, until colooured and slightly blackened, then add the garlic and fry for a minute more, until fragrant.

Turn down the heat to medium, squeeze in the tomato puree and cook for one minute, until the mix darkens. Season generously, then tip in the rice and toast for a minute. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and chicken stock, and bring to a bubble.

articles.title: Guerlain 101: From Rouge G to Abeille Royale, the Products That Define the French Beauty House
articles.summary: Nearly 200 years old, Guerlain remains relevant by being obsessed with innovation. Discover Vogue's edit of the best Guerlain products, from cult-favorite lipsticks to honey-powered skincare.
body: Guerlain has been a fixture of French luxury beauty for nearly 200 years. In an industry where new brands seem to appear overnight, maintaining that kind of longevity, and staying relevant throughout, is no small feat. As you can imagine, this has meant a lot of product launches; but according to the brand not every new idea is rushed to market.

“We take our time at Guerlain, waiting until we have something truly meaningful to offer the world,” CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis tells Vogue. “When you’re a house that has been passionate about fragrance and cosmetics for 200 years, you are obsessed with innovating.”

One area this innovation has played out is Guerlain’s work with honey. For more than 15 years, Guerlain has developed a multi-parameter selection process to identify honeys with increasingly powerful repair activities, per Dr. Frédéric Bonté, Guerlain’s director of scientific communication. The research is far more involved than simply identifying different varieties of honey: It includes studying honeybees, analyzing the composition of the honey they produce, and examining the environments in which they live.
points: Nearly 200 years old, Guerlain remains relevant by being obsessed with innovation.

articles.title: Asanas at Sea? The Best Places for Yoga Around the World Are Also the Most Unconventional
articles.summary: From a rocky mountainside to the middle of the ocean, explore these singular places to practice your suryanamaskars.
body: The best places for yoga are at once picturesque and contemplative, whether it be pranayama in Ladakh’s austere landscape, dhanurasana in the thick of Thailand’s jungles, or shavasana beside an Alpine lake in New Zealand. These experiences offer as much external peace as they do internal, and even long after the session and trip have ended, it's those stirring, outdoor moments that endure. They feel like they’ve stopped time and are worth going out of the way for—planned or spontaneous. And what's better than practicing your asanas in a phenomenal natural setting? With these 10 best places for yoga, grab your go-to mat and embrace your inner yogini.

The middle of the Indian Ocean is possibly the most unique spot one can find to do yoga. Practice asanas while sailing on a traditional wooden dhow at this Maldivian resort. Lux* South Ari Atoll organizes this cruise at golden hour with an instructor guiding you on Tibetan Sound Bowl therapy, breathwork, and yoga. Sip on a refreshing drink, inhale a mood-enhancing oil blend, and float on the waves as you meditate and feel your mind reset.
